newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Southeast power prices mixed ahead of cold.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Southeast power prices mixed ahead of cold.

text.p: Spot bulk electricity prices in the southeastern U.S. were on either side of unchanged Thursday, as cold weather moved toward the region and a South Carolina nuke unit was expected to go off line, sources said.

Firm, peak power in the northern part of the Tennessee Valley Authority (TVA) territory for Friday delivery traded in the $21.00-22.00 per megawatt hour (MWh) range, down from Wednesday's $22.00-23.00 range.
Firm, off-peak electricity in northern TVA was assessed in the $14.00-15.00 range, as compared with $15 seen on Wednesday.

At the Georgia/Florida border, prices for firm, peak electricity in 16 hour blocks for Friday delivery were quoted mostly in the $24.50-25.50 per MWh range, up from Wednesday's $23.00-24.00 trading range.
Firm, off-peak power for Friday at the Ga./Fla. border was still notionally assessed around $16.00-17.00.
Temperatures in the Southeast are expected to begin dropping late Saturday, with temperatures about four to 12 degrees Fahrenheit below-normal anticipated by early next week.
Separately, Duke Power will take the 1,129 megawatt Catawba nuclear power unit in Clover, S.C., off line at 2000 EST Thursday due to an unidentified leak, the Nuclear Regulatory Commission reported.
The company, operator of the plant with a 25 percent share, was not immediately available for comment.
